title: Responsive & Zoom-Friendly Layouts 📐
description: Create layouts that work on any screen, at any zoom level, without breaking.

slides.title: Why Zoom Matters 🔍
slides.content:
WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text): Users must be able to zoom to **200%** without loss of content or functionality.

* This means no horizontal scrolling at 320px wide (equivalent to 1280px at 200% zoom).
* Layouts must be **fluid** and adapt gracefully.

Low‑vision users rely heavily on browser zoom.

quizData.question: What is the minimum zoom level a website must support without horizontal scrolling (AA requirement)?
quizData.explanation: WCAG 1.4.4 requires content to be functional at 200% zoom.

slides.title: Fluid Layouts & Relative Units 📐
slides.content:
Avoid fixed widths in pixels. Instead:

* Use `%`, `vw`, `rem`, `em` for widths.
* `max-width` on containers to prevent lines from becoming too long.
* `min()` / `max()` / `clamp()` for modern responsive typography and spacing.

**Example**: `width: min(100%, 60ch);` – container fills screen but never exceeds a comfortable reading length.

slides.title: Fluid Typography

quizData.question: Which CSS unit scales relative to the user's default font size?
quizData.explanation: `rem` (root em) scales with the root font size, respecting the user's browser settings.

slides.title: Media Queries: Beyond Width 📱
slides.content:
Don't just use `@media (max-width: ...)`. Accessibility media queries:

* **prefers-reduced-motion** – adapt animations.
* **prefers-color-scheme** – dark/light mode.
* **prefers-contrast** – high contrast mode.
* **forced-colors** – Windows High Contrast Mode.

These let your site respect the user's system settings.

quizData.question: What does `forced-colors: active` indicate?

options.text: The user has enabled dark mode
Windows High Contrast Mode is active

quizData.explanation: `forced-colors` is a CSS media feature that matches when Windows High Contrast Mode (or similar) is enabled.

slides.title: Testing Responsiveness 🧪
slides.content:
* Zoom your browser to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd + +).
* Resize the viewport to 320px width (smallest phone).
* Check that no content is cut off or requires horizontal scrolling.
* Use the browser's device toolbar to emulate various screens.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Mobile First
Design for the smallest screen first, then add complexity for larger breakpoints. This forces you to prioritise content and keep layouts simple.
